question:
Given below are the two columns. Columns A has the feature and Column B has the details.

 Column A (Feature) Column B (Detail)
 a. Ochre-coloured pottery i. Found in association with copper hoards
 b. Upper Gangetic basin ii. Region with most copper hoard discoveries
 c. Settled agriculturists and artisans iii. Users of copper hoards in the doab region
 d. Plateau regions of Bihar and neighbouring areas iv. Secondary site of copper hoard findings
solution:
The correct answer is __**a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv**__.

**__Key Points__**

• **Ochre-coloured pottery (OCP)** is a **Late Bronze Age** ceramic culture that flourished in the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** between **2000 BCE and 1500 BCE**. In archaeological excavations, **OCP** is frequently found in direct association with **copper hoards**, suggesting a shared cultural context. *Hence, match a-i is correct.*

• The **Upper Gangetic basin**, particularly the **Ganga-Yamuna Doab**, is recognized as the primary region with the **most copper hoard discoveries**. This region has yielded a vast array of specialized copper implements, indicating it was the core center of this metallurgical tradition. *Hence, match b-ii is correct.*

• The **users of copper hoards in the doab region** were primarily **settled agriculturists and artisans**. Evidence from sites like **Saipai** indicates that these people lived in established settlements, practiced **agriculture** (cultivating crops like **rice** and **barley**), and maintained a sophisticated **artisanal** class capable of advanced **metalworking**. *Hence, match c-iii is correct.*
